mainTopic: Warnings (התראה and קינוי) in the סוטה laws: whether an עוברת על דת needs a warning to lose her כתובה, and whether and when a husband can cancel his קינוי.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: שמואל shows his view about a יבמה works even according to רבי יאשיה. Then the גמרא asks whether an עוברת על דת needs a warning before she loses her כתובה. Several proofs from our משנה are pushed off. רב חנינא מסורא's proof from the court's warning is accepted: a warning is needed. Next the גמרא asks whether a husband may keep such a wife if he wants to. Its proof is pushed off. It then asks whether a husband can cancel his קינוי, and after two rejected proofs, רבי יאשיה's report from זעירא shows that he can. רב אחא and רבינא argue whether cancelling works even after סתירה. The גמרא proves from the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי that after סתירה it does not. Finally the גמרא turns to the משנה about husbands who died before their wives drank, and begins explaining בית שמאי's reasoning: a document that stands to be collected counts as already collected.

steps.title: שמואל's view works even according to רבי יאשיה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל defends his position by showing it fits even רבי יאשיה, who includes a יבמה in the סוטה process through a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל could say: I hold my view even according to רבי יאשיה. Since the פסוק had to specially include her, that shows she is not really his wife at all in other matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by showing that שמואל can defend his view even according to רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה learns from a פסוק that a יבמה who lived with her יבם is treated like a wife for the סוטה process. שמואל turns this into a point in his favor: if a פסוק was needed to include her, then without it she would not count as his wife. So in every other area, she is not considered his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who includes a יבמה in the סוטה process through a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: When a פסוק is needed to include a case, that can show the case would not be included without it. So the rule applies only where the פסוק says.

phrases.english: And Shmuel could say:
What I said holds even according to Rabbi Yoshiya.
Since the verse was needed to include her,
phrases.notes: "Her" is the יבמה who lived with her יבם, the woman רבי יאשיה includes from the פסוק.

phrases.english: that shows she is not his wife at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי — אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about שמואל and רבי יאשיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the opposing source into support: the need for a special פסוק shows the יבמה is otherwise not a wife.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יאשיה's inclusion of a יבמה seemed to treat her as a full wife, which would go against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inclusion covers only what the פסוק says. Otherwise she is not his wife at all.

steps.title: Does a woman who breaks modesty rules need a warning to lose her כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: does an עוברת על דת lose her כתובה only after a warning, or even without one?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a woman who breaks the rules of modesty, does she need a warning to lose her כתובה, or not? Do we say that since she is breaking the rules, she needs no warning? Or perhaps she needs a warning, so that if she wants to stop, she will stop?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question and gives the reasoning for both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: she already knows her behavior is wrong, so a warning adds nothing. Side two: a warning gives her a chance to stop before she loses her כתובה. The question is whether the warning is there to inform her or to give her a chance to do תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
A woman who breaks the rules of modesty
To make her lose her כתובה
She turns back from her behavior

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
A woman who breaks the rules of modesty,
does she need a warning in order to lose her kesubah,
or does she not need one?
Do we say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעוֹבֶרֶת עַל דָּת הִיא — לָא בָּעֲיָא הַתְרָאָה,
phrases.english: since she is breaking the rules, she does not need a warning,
or perhaps she does need a warning,
so that if she wants to turn back, she will turn back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to שמואל's point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a warning is required before an עוברת על דת loses her כתובה.

steps.title: Attempted proof from the משנה about an ארוסה and שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from our משנה that a warning is needed for losing the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink and do not collect a כתובה. So drinking is what she does not do, but he can still warn her. For what purpose? Is it not to make her lose her כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה as a possible answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these women do not drink, which suggests they can still be warned. Since the warning cannot lead to drinking, it must have some other purpose, and the obvious one is losing the כתובה. If so, a warning is needed before she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A widow waiting for her יבם

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself never mentions a warning. The גמרא reads it in from the wording: if the משנה only says "she does not drink," a warning must still be possible.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A betrothed woman and a widow waiting for her yavam
do not drink and do not collect a kesubah.
Drinking is what she does not do,
but he can still warn her.
For what purpose?
Is it not to make her lose her kesubah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a warning is required before a woman loses her כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם do not drink and do not collect a כתובה.

steps.title: אביי: the warning makes her forbidden to him
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The warning's purpose is to make her forbidden to the man, not to take away her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No. The warning is to make her forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down the proof by giving the warning a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she ignores the warning and secludes herself with the other man, she becomes forbidden to her ארוס or יבם. Since that explains why the warning matters, the משנה tells us nothing about the כתובה. The question is settled later, in steps 8-9.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her forbidden to him

phrases.english: Abaye said: No,
it is to make her forbidden to him.
phrases.notes: He means: if she secludes herself after the warning, she becomes forbidden to the man who warned her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the warning must be about the כתובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof missed another purpose for the warning: making her forbidden to him.

steps.title: רב פפא: the warning lets her drink after the marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives another way out of the proof. The warning can cause her to drink later, once she is married, and a ברייתא supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the warning is to make her drink once she is married. As a ברייתא teaches: we do not warn an ארוסה to make her drink while she is still an ארוסה, but we do warn an ארוסה to make her drink once she is married.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a second answer to the proof and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says she cannot drink while she is still an ארוסה. A warning given now still counts later, so if she secludes herself after the marriage, she drinks. Since that is the warning's purpose, the proof about the כתובה falls away. The question is settled later, in steps 8-9.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her drink the bitter water
As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רב פפא show that the warning to an ארוסה or שומרת יבם has a purpose other than the כתובה. So the משנה does not settle whether an עוברת על דת needs a warning.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
it is to make her drink once she is married.
As it is taught in a baraita:
We do not warn a betrothed woman
to make her drink while she is still betrothed,
but we do warn a betrothed woman
to make her drink once she is married.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְהַשְׁקוֹתָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא נְשׂוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different rejection of the proof in step 3, alongside אביי's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the warning must be about the כתובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The warning can work later, to make her drink after she is married, as the ברייתא states.

steps.title: Proof from women in forbidden marriages who can still be warned
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה that women in forbidden marriages don't drink and don't collect a כתובה. He reasons that they can still be warned. Since the warning can't be needed to forbid them to their husbands, it must be about losing the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. A widow married to a כהן גדול, a divorcee or חלוצה married to a regular כהן, a ממזרת or נתינה married to a regular Jew, or a regular Jewish woman married to a ממזר or נתין: they don't drink and don't collect a כתובה. So drinking is what they don't do, but they can still be warned. For what purpose? If it is to forbid them to the husband, they are already forbidden to him. So it must be to make them lose their כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new proof that a warning is needed before a woman loses her כתובה. He uses the next part of the משנה about women in forbidden marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says these women don't drink, which suggests they can still be warned. A warning normally makes a woman forbidden to her husband, but these women are already forbidden to theirs. So, says רבא, the warning's only job left is to take away the כתובה, which shows a warning is what makes her lose it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a proof
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A woman released from יבום through חליצה. She is forbidden to a כהן.
A woman born from a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew
A woman descended from the גבעונים, who may not marry a regular Jew

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a חלוצה married to a common priest,
a ממזרת or a Gibeonite woman married to a regular Jew,
a regular Jewish woman married to a ממזר or a Gibeonite man:
they do not drink and do not collect a כתובה.
phrases.notes: "Drink" means the bitter water of the סוטה test.

phrases.english: It is drinking that she does not do,
but warning, he does warn them.
And for what purpose?
If it is to forbid them to him,
they are already forbidden!
Rather, is it not to make them lose their כתובה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof (Steps 3-5) was pushed off, רבא brings a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That an עוברת על דת loses her כתובה only after a warning
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about women in forbidden marriages, plus the reasoning that their warning can't be meant to forbid them to the husband

steps.title: The warning forbids her to the other man
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא answers that the warning has another purpose. It forbids her to the other man, just as a warned and secluded woman is forbidden to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא said: No. The warning is to make her forbidden to the other man, just as she would be to the husband. As we learned in a משנה: just as she is forbidden to the husband, so too she is forbidden to the other man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא pushes off רבא's proof. He shows the warning does have a use other than the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the warning had nothing left to do except take away the כתובה. רב יהודה points to another result: if she secludes herself after the warning, she becomes forbidden to the man she was alone with. He backs this up with a משנה, so the proof no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: The other man she is suspected with
As we learned in a משנה: introduces a quote from a משנה
Just as... so too: a direct comparison

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Diskarta said: No,
the warning is to forbid her to the other man, just like to the husband.
As we learned in a משנה: Just as she is forbidden to the husband,
so too she is forbidden to the other man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off רבא's proof in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's proof is rejected. The question itself is settled in steps 8-9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the warning had no other use, but it can forbid her to the other man.

steps.title: Proof from the court's warning, which is only about the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא quotes the משנה about women whom the court warns on the husband's behalf. That warning is said to be only to disqualify her from her כתובה, not to make her drink. This shows that losing the כתובה depends on a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא מסורא said: Come and hear. These are the women the court warns: a woman whose husband became deaf-mute or lost his sanity, or was locked in prison. The court's warning was not said in order to make her drink, but in order to disqualify her from her כתובה. Learn from this that a warning is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא מסורא brings a third proof, from the court's warning in the משנה, that a warning is needed to lose the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה itself says the purpose of the warning: not the bitter water, only the כתובה. If a woman could lose her כתובה without any warning, the court would not need to warn her for that. So losing the כתובה must depend on a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: The court gives the warning in place of the husband
To make her drink the bitter water
To disqualify her from her כתובה

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof works where the earlier ones failed, because the משנה itself tells us the warning's only purpose.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: תָּא שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina of Sura said: Come and hear:
And these are the women to whom the court issues a warning:
one whose husband became a deaf-mute, or lost his sanity,
or was locked up in prison.
And they did not say this in order to make her drink,
but in order to disqualify her from her כתובה.
Learn from this: a warning is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's proof was pushed off in Step 7, a new proof is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That an עוברת על דת needs a warning before she loses her כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the court's warning, which says it is only for the כתובה

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב חנינא מסורא's proof. A warning is needed before an עוברת על דת loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated words שמע מינה show the גמרא accepting the proof, with no answer against it. This settles the question from Step 2: losing the כתובה requires a warning first.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the גמרא accepts the proof

steps.whatToRemember: An עוברת על דת loses her כתובה only after she has been warned. The proof comes from the court's warning, whose only purpose is the כתובה.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A warning is needed for an עוברת על דת to lose her כתובה.

steps.title: Why did the others not use this proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the other אמוראים did not bring the clear proof that רב חנינא מסורא brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the others: why did they not bring their proof from this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the earlier attempts. It asks why the other אמוראים did not use רב חנינא מסורא's clear source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנינא מסורא's משנה says outright that the warning is there to take away the כתובה. So it is strange that the others brought weaker proofs that were pushed off. The גמרא wants to know what they saw as weak about this source.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them (the other אמוראים who tried to bring proofs)

phrases.english: And all of them, what is the reason
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the אמוראים in the earlier steps whose proofs were pushed off.

phrases.english: that they did not bring the proof from this?
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה רב חנינא מסורא quoted, about women the court warns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the accepted proof and asks why the earlier אמוראים passed over it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the earlier אמוראים did not use the clear משנה about the court's warning.

steps.title: That case may be special: she does not fear her husband
steps.stepSummary: The others may have thought the court's warning is a special case, because these women have no fear of their husbands at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because she has no fear of her husband at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The others may have felt that the משנה about the court's warning only applies to an unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband is a deaf-mute, insane, or in prison, the wife has no fear of him at all. In that case a warning might be needed before she loses her כתובה. In an ordinary marriage, she may lose it even without a warning, so this משנה could not prove a general rule.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
since she has no fear of the husband at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing why the earlier אמוראים saw this source as a special case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court's warning case is unusual, because the wife has no fear of her husband at all. A warning may be needed there but not in ordinary cases.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא concluded that a warning is needed before an עוברת על דת loses her כתובה. The other אמוראים just saw the court-warning case as possibly special, since the wife has no fear of her husband.

steps.title: May a husband keep a wife who breaks the religious standard?
steps.stepSummary: New question: if a woman is an עוברת על דת and her husband wants to stay married to her, may he?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if a woman breaks the religious standard and her husband wants to keep her, may he keep her or not? Do we say the Torah made it depend on the husband's objection, and this husband does not object? Or perhaps, since there is an objection (from the Torah), it counts as an objection?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question. Does a husband have to divorce an עוברת על דת, or may he keep her if he does not mind?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sides: maybe the rule only exists because the husband objects, so if he does not mind he may keep her. Or maybe the Torah itself objects to this behavior. Then it counts as if the husband objects, no matter what he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (an open question among the Sages)
A woman who breaks the religious standard of modest behavior
To keep her (stay married to her)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
A woman who breaks the religious standard
and the husband wants to keep her,
may he keep her, or may he not keep her?
Do we say that on the husband's objection
the Torah made it depend, and this one does not object?
Or perhaps, since there is an objection, it counts as an objection?
phrases.notes: He means the Torah itself objects to this behavior, so it is treated as if the husband objects.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוֹבֶרֶת עַל דָּת וְרָצָה בַּעַל לְקַיְּימָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the כתובה question and opens a new question about whether the husband may stay married to her.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule against keeping an עוברת על דת depends on the husband's feelings or on the Torah's own objection.

steps.title: Proof from the court warning in the husband's place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that he may not keep her. The court warns women for their husbands, and the court would not do something the husband might not want.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: These are the women the court warns: one whose husband became a deaf-mute, became insane, or was put in prison. If you say a husband who wants to keep her may keep her, would the court do something the husband might not want?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same משנה from step 8 to answer the new question. It argues that he may not keep her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court steps in and warns the wife without asking the husband. If a husband were allowed to keep her, maybe this husband would not want her warned. Since the court acts anyway, it seems the husband's wishes do not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Warn (give the formal warning to a wife)
He is not happy with it

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And these are the women whom the court warns:
one whose husband became a deaf-mute, or became insane,
or who was locked in prison.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ רָצָה בַּעַל לְקַיְּימָהּ מְקַיְּימָהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say that if the husband wants to keep her, he may keep her,
would the court do something
that perhaps the husband is not happy with?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁבֵּית דִּין מְקַנִּין לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 12 from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband may not keep an עוברת על דת, even if he wants to.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing women whom the court warns in place of their husbands.

steps.title: Normally a husband would want her warned
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: in the normal case, a husband is glad to have such a wife warned, so the court can act for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ordinary situation is: since she breaks the religious standard, he is surely happy with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from step 13. The court is not going against the husband; it is doing what most husbands would want.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court can act because almost any husband would want a wife who acts this way to be warned. So the court's warning shows nothing about a husband who really wants to keep her. The question from step 12 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: The ordinary situation, the usual case
He is surely happy with it

phrases.english: The ordinary situation is:
since she is one who breaks the religious standard,
he is surely happy with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question of step 12 is not decided either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The court acts because a typical husband would want the warning, not because the husband's wishes do not count.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not rule that a husband may keep her. It only shows the משנה does not prove that he may not.

steps.title: Can a husband cancel his warning?
steps.stepSummary: New question: if a husband warned his wife (קינוי) and then took the warning back, is the warning cancelled?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a husband who cancelled his warning, is the warning cancelled or not? Do we say the Torah made it depend on the husband's warning, and he cancelled it? Or perhaps, since he warned her at the start, he cannot cancel it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens another new question about the husband's warning. Can he take back a קינוי once he has given it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: the whole סוטה process starts with the husband's warning, so if he cancels it, it is gone. Other side: once he has warned her, the warning has taken effect and he can no longer undo it. After two proofs are pushed off, step 20 answers this and step 22 concludes it.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's formal warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
A husband who cancelled his warning:
is his warning cancelled, or is it not cancelled?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן בְּקִינּוּי דְּבַעַל תְּלָא רַחֲמָנָא,
phrases.english: Do we say the Torah made it depend on the husband's warning,
and the husband has cancelled his warning,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּקַנִּי לַיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא —
phrases.english: or perhaps, since he warned her at the start,
he cannot cancel it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בַּעַל שֶׁמָּחַל עַל קִינּוּיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the husband's power over his own warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband's קינוי can be cancelled once given.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the warning can be cancelled, the husband can stop the סוטה process before it starts. If not, the warning stays in force even against his wishes.

steps.title: Proof from the court warning on the husband's behalf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that a husband cannot cancel his קינוי. If he could, the court would never give a warning that the husband might later cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: These are the women the court warns for their husbands: a woman whose husband became a חרש, became a שוטה, or was in prison. If a husband could cancel his warning, would the court do something the husband could come along and cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first proof for the question from step 15. It argues that a husband cannot cancel his warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court warns women whose husbands cannot do it themselves. If the husband could later cancel that warning, the court's action could be undone by him, and that seems improper for a court. So, the גמרא suggests, a husband's cancellation must not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an opening for a proof
They give a קינוי (formal warning not to be alone with a certain man)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה used in step 13, but now it is used for a different question: not keeping an עוברת על דת, but cancelling a קינוי.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
And these are the women whom the court warns:
one whose husband became a deaf-mute, or became mentally unfit,
or was locked up in prison.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בַּעַל שֶׁמָּחַל עַל קִינּוּיוֹ —
phrases.english: And if you say that a husband who cancelled his warning,
his warning is cancelled,

phrases.aramaic: עָבְדִינַן מִידֵּי דְּאָתֵי בַּעַל מָחֵיל לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: would we do something that the husband can come and cancel?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁבֵּית דִּין מְקַנִּין לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First attempt to answer the question in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: A husband cannot cancel his קינוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing women the court warns for their husbands.

steps.title: People normally agree with the court
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Usually a husband goes along with what the court did, so the court is not worried that he will cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Normally, a person agrees with the court's decision.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a husband has the power to cancel, in real life he will not cancel what the court did. So the court can still act without worry. The משנה does not prove that cancelling is impossible.

phrases.english: The ordinary situation is:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַסְכִּים עַל דַּעַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: a person agrees with the opinion of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question is answered in steps 20-22.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the husband would really cancel. In practice he goes along with the court.

steps.title: Proof from the two scholars sent along
steps.stepSummary: The court sends two scholars with the husband so he will not be with his wife on the way. If he could just cancel the warning, why would the guards be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The court gives him two תלמידי חכמים in case he is with her on the way. If a husband could cancel his warning, let him cancel it and be with her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof that a husband cannot cancel his warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escorts are there to stop a forbidden act. If cancelling the קינוי made being together allowed, the whole guard system would seem pointless. So the גמרא suggests cancelling must not work.

keyTerms.meaning: He will be with her (marital relations)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And they give him two Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: This is when the husband brings his wife up to ירושלים to drink the water.

phrases.english: in case he is with her on the way.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בַּעַל שֶׁמָּחַל עַל קִינּוּיוֹ — קִינּוּיוֹ מָחוּל,
phrases.english: And if you say a husband who cancelled his warning, his warning is cancelled,
let him cancel his warning and be with her!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וּמוֹסְרִין לוֹ שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer step 15, after the first proof was pushed off.
steps.raayaObject: A husband cannot cancel his קינוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about sending two scholars with the husband.

steps.title: Scholars are sent so they can guide him
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Scholars are chosen because they know the law. If he wants to be with her, they tell him to cancel the warning first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically Torah scholars? Because they are learned. If he wants to be with her, they tell him: cancel your warning, and then be with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof. It shows the escorts fit well with the idea that he can cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The escorts are not there to block him. They are there to make sure he does it the allowed way, by cancelling the קינוי first. That explains why they must be scholars and not just any guards.

phrases.english: Why specifically Torah scholars?
Because they are learned,
so that if he wants to be with her, they say to him:
Cancel your warning, and then be with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely; the escorts fit with cancelling being allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the escorts stop him altogether. Really they teach him to cancel first.

steps.title: זעירא's three teachings: the warning can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה reports three teachings from זעירא. The first one says outright that a husband who cancels his קינוי has cancelled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יאשיה said: זעירא, one of the men of ירושלים, told me three things. A husband who cancels his warning, it is cancelled. A זקן ממרא whom the court wants to forgive, they may forgive him. A בן סורר ומורה whose father and mother want to forgive him, they may forgive him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clear teaching that answers the question from step 15: the husband can cancel his warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier proofs, this source says the rule directly, so no side reasoning is needed. It groups three cases where the party with authority over the case (the husband, the court, the parents) may choose to forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder who rules against the High Court

steps.whatToRemember: A husband who cancels his קינוי has cancelled it. זעירא also taught that a זקן ממרא can be forgiven by the court and a בן סורר ומורה by his parents, but the next step shows the scholars of the South rejected the teaching about the זקן ממרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question opened in step 15. It shows that the קינוי depends on the husband's will, so he can also undo it.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Yoshiya said:
Three things were told to me by
Ze'eira, one of the men of Jerusalem:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל שֶׁמָּחַל עַל קִינּוּיוֹ — קִינּוּיוֹ מָחוּל,
phrases.english: A husband who cancelled his warning, his warning is cancelled;

phrases.aramaic: וְזָקֵן מַמְרֵא שֶׁרָצוּ בֵּית דִּין לִמְחוֹל לוֹ — מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: and a rebellious elder whom the court wanted to forgive, they may forgive him;
and a stubborn and rebellious son

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁרָצוּ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ לִמְחוֹל לוֹ — מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ.
phrases.english: whose father and mother wanted to forgive him, they may forgive him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two rejected proofs against cancelling, a direct source proves that cancelling works.
steps.raayaObject: A husband can cancel his קינוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה quoting זעירא of ירושלים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband who cancels his קינוי has cancelled it.

steps.title: The southern colleagues agreed on two of the three teachings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה reports that his colleagues in the South accepted two of זעירא's three teachings, including the one about the husband cancelling his קינוי. They did not accept that a זקן ממרא can be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I went to my friends in the South, they agreed with me about two of the teachings. About the rebellious elder they did not agree, so that arguments would not grow among the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from step 20 continues. רבי יאשיה says the scholars of the South accepted the husband-cancelling teaching too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the proof stronger. The rule that a husband can cancel his קינוי was not just one person's opinion; other scholars agreed to it. Only the teaching about the זקן ממרא was turned down, for a separate reason: they did not want disputes to spread.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder who rules against the high court

phrases.english: And when I came to my colleagues in the South,
they agreed with me about two,
phrases.notes: The two are two of זעירא's three teachings. One of them is that a husband can cancel his קינוי.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל זָקֵן מַמְרֵא לֹא הוֹדוּ לִי
phrases.english: but about the rebellious elder they did not agree with me
so that disputes should not multiply in Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted as proof in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband can cancel his קינוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's report that the southern scholars accepted this teaching.

steps.title: Conclusion: the husband's cancellation works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that a husband who cancels his קינוי has really cancelled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a husband who cancels his warning, his warning is cancelled. Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רבי יאשיה's report and confirms it. The question from step 15 is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs against cancelling (steps 16 and 18) were pushed off. This proof for cancelling is clear and accepted. So the rule stands: the husband can take back his warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: A husband can cancel his קינוי, and the cancellation works.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
a husband who cancelled his warning —
his warning is cancelled.
Indeed, learn it from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בַּעַל שֶׁמָּחַל עַל קִינּוּיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in steps 20-21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband who cancels his קינוי has really cancelled it.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא argue about cancelling after seclusion
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue over how far the rule reaches. One says cancelling works only before סתירה. The other says it works even after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says: before she was secluded, the warning is cancelled, but after she was secluded, it is not cancelled. The other says: even after she was secluded, it is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a husband can cancel, the גמרא brings a dispute about when he can do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before סתירה nothing has happened yet, so the husband can easily drop the warning. After סתירה, the wife may already be forbidden to him. The question is whether he can still undo that.

keyTerms.meaning: Seclusion: the wife being alone with the man she was warned about

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a husband can cancel before סתירה. They argue only about cancelling after סתירה.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
One says:
before seclusion — it is cancelled,
after seclusion — it is not cancelled.
And one says:
after seclusion, it is also cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule from step 22 and asks how far it reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: one view says cancelling works only before סתירה; the other says it also works after סתירה.

steps.title: The גמרא favors the view that cancelling after seclusion does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is more reasonable to hold that after סתירה the warning cannot be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes sense to follow the one who says it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks a side in the dispute. This sets up the next move, where it will prove its choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a claim, not yet a proof. The גמרא states which view it thinks is right. Right after, it will ask 'how do we know?' and bring a source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense

phrases.english: And it is reasonable to follow the one who says it is not cancelled,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After סתירה, the husband's cancellation does not work.

steps.title: How do we know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that shows cancelling does not work after סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the claim it just made. It is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'it makes sense' is not enough. The גמרא wants a real source to back it up.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the claim in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a husband cannot cancel his קינוי after סתירה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי says the husband can be trusted with his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by pointing to how the רבנן replied to רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי argued with a קל וחומר: a husband is trusted alone with his wife when she is a נדה, a כרת prohibition. So he should surely be trusted with a סוטה, which is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know it from how the רבנן answered רבי יוסי. As it was taught: רבי יוסי says, her husband is trusted with her, from a קל וחומר. If with a נדה, which is a כרת sin, her husband is trusted with her, then with a סוטה, which is only a regular prohibition, surely he is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. First it brings רבי יוסי's argument, which the רבנן will reply to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says there is no need for the scholars from step 18 to travel with the couple. Husbands are trusted to be alone with a נדה wife, even though that sin is more severe. So they can be trusted with a סוטה, whose sin is lighter. The proof itself will come from the רבנן's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
A very severe punishment: being cut off

phrases.english: From how the Rabbis answered Rabbi Yosei.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
her husband is trusted with her,
phrases.notes: He means the husband can be alone with her on the way to the בית המקדש, so the scholars from step 18 aren't needed.

phrases.english: from a קל וחומר:
just as a נדה, who is under כרת —
her husband is trusted with her,
a סוטה, who is only under a regular prohibition,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 25 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the ברייתא in which the רבנן reply to רבי יוסי's קל וחומר.

steps.title: The רבנן answer: a סוטה has no way to become permitted
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי יוסי's קל וחומר. A נדה will become permitted later, so her husband can wait. A סוטה may never become permitted. This shows that after סתירה the husband cannot simply cancel the warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. If you say this about a נדה, that is because she has a way to become permitted. Will you say it about a סוטה, who has no way to become permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן break רבי יוסי's קל וחומר. Their reason is the proof the גמרא was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a סוטה 'has no היתר.' If the husband could cancel his warning after סתירה, she would have an easy היתר: he could just cancel it. So the רבנן must hold that after סתירה, cancelling does not work. This supports the view the גמרא chose in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say this about one case, will you say it about the other? (a formula for rejecting a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: Once סתירה has happened, the husband can no longer cancel his קינוי. That is why the רבנן say a סוטה has no היתר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear limit on the rule from step 22. Cancelling works before סתירה but not after it.

phrases.english: They said to him:
No, if you say so about a נדה —
that is because she has a way to become permitted,
will you say so about a סוטה —
who has no way to become permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן refute רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from step 26. Their reason supplies the proof asked for in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי's קל וחומר comparing a סוטה to a נדה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The husband is trusted with a נדה because she will become permitted, not because her sin is lighter or heavier. A סוטה has no such היתר.
steps.raayaObject: That cancelling the קינוי after סתירה does not work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's statement that a סוטה has no היתר. If cancelling worked after סתירה, she would have one.

steps.title: Why the רבנן's answer proves cancelling fails after seclusion
steps.stepSummary: If the husband could cancel his warning after סתירה, the סוטה would have a way to become permitted. That goes against the רבנן's claim that she may never become permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that after the seclusion the warning can be cancelled, then you have found a way for her to become permitted: if he wants, he cancels his warning and lives with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי proves the point. If cancelling worked after סתירה, the רבנן's argument would not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said a סוטה is different from a נדה because a סוטה may never become permitted. If the husband could cancel his warning after סתירה, she would always have a simple way to become permitted. So the רבנן must hold that cancelling does not work at that stage.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelled, forgiven (here: the warning is withdrawn)
The husband's warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ לְאַחַר סְתִירָה מָחוּל לָהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say that after seclusion the warning is cancelled for her,
you find that she has a way to become permitted,
phrases.notes: This goes straight against what the רבנן just said in step 27, that a סוטה may never become permitted.

phrases.english: for if he wants, he cancels his warning
and lives with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ לְאַחַר סְתִירָה מָחוּל לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the רבנן's rejection of רבי יוסי in step 27 serves as the source asked for in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a husband cannot cancel his warning after סתירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's reply to רבי יוסי that a סוטה may never become permitted

steps.title: Conclusion: after seclusion the warning cannot be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that after סתירה the husband's warning cannot be cancelled, and confirms this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: after the seclusion, the warning cannot be cancelled. Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the proof and then confirms it with a final 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the argument between רב אחא and רבינא from step 23. The view that cancelling works only before סתירה is now proven from the רבנן. After סתירה the case is locked in, and the husband cannot undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the גמרא's formula for drawing or confirming a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: A husband can cancel his warning before his wife is secluded with the man, but not after. Once סתירה has happened, she cannot become permitted just because he cancels.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
after seclusion, the warning is not cancelled.
Indeed, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion that follows from the proof in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After סתירה, the husband's warning cannot be cancelled.

steps.title: New line in the משנה: the husbands died before the women drank
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about women whose husbands died before they drank the bitter water, where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if their husbands died before they drank, בית שמאי say, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say these women collect their כתובה and do not drink. בית הלל say they either drink or lose their כתובה. The 'etc.' points to that full dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: They drank (the bitter water of the סוטה)
Short for 'etc.': the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: If their husbands died before they drank,
בית שמאי say, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: בית שמאי say they collect their כתובה and don't drink. בית הלל say they drink or don't collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of cancelling the warning and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about whether a סוטה whose husband died before she drank collects her כתובה.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know the principle that drives each opinion, not just the ruling. Once that principle is found, the whole dispute will make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? The גמרא's standard question for finding the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.title: בית שמאי: a document ready to be collected counts as already collected
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that a document that stands to be collected is treated as if it were already collected. So the woman counts as already holding her כתובה money.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold: a document that stands to be collected is considered as if it were already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by giving בית שמאי's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she holds the כתובה document, the money counts as already hers. The heirs would have to prove she sinned in order to take it away. Since the husband is dead, she cannot drink to clear herself, but she still keeps the money.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document, here the כתובה
Is considered as if already collected

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean she has actually received the money yet. It means the law treats her as if she already holds it, so the heirs are the ones who must prove their case.
